relations.subject: Murray Barnson Emeneau
relations.object: Department of Linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley
relations.evidence: Murray Barnson Emeneau (February 28, 1904 – August 29, 2005) was a Canadian-American linguist and the founder of the Department of Linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley.

relations.subject: Murray Barnson Emeneau
relations.evidence: Emeneau was awarded a Rhodes Scholarship to Balliol College at Oxford University.

relations.subject: Murray Barnson Emeneau
relations.evidence: From Oxford he arrived at Yale University in 1926, where he took a teaching appointment in Latin.

relations.subject: Murray Barnson Emeneau
relations.evidence: While at Yale, Emeneau began Sanskrit and Indo-European studies with the Sanskritist Franklin Edgerton and Indo-Europeanist Edgar Sturtevant.
